limitations: Synthetic asynchronous wait is not CPU work or model inference.
Synthetic CPU iterations and touched memory allocation are fixed work controls, not calibrated model workloads.
Shared host; generator competes with system under test. No hardware isolation claim.
cgroup counters are observational and sampled at 100 ms; the resource endpoint adds small control-plane work outside the business payload.
A configured isolation label is descriptive; observed cgroup CPU/memory limits in the manifest and resources file are authoritative.
Component resource caps do not equalize aggregate architecture budgets; remote topologies can use harness and specialist quotas while local work shares one quota.
cgroup memory.peak is container-lifetime state; sampled memory.current and RSS provide round-scoped observations but can miss activity between samples.
Body bytes exclude TCP/IP and HTTP headers. Serialization metric covers explicit domain codec only.
A2A uses immediate Message replies; durable task lifecycle, polling and discovery cost are excluded. Explicitly configured application retries are included.
OTel enabled includes synchronous local JSONL export; not a universal instrumentation overhead.
No image digest for native subprocess runs; null means not used/not measured.
MCP request/response bytes are explicit tool arguments, text results and resource URI/content bytes; JSON-RPC/HTTP framing and headers are excluded.
The MCP stdio SDK does not expose its child PID through the public client API; specialist CPU/RSS are therefore unavailable for that arm.
v0.3 fault injection is deterministic application-layer treatment, not a proxy for every network, host or process failure mode.
Idempotency state is bounded, in-memory and worker-local; it is not a durable cross-worker guarantee.
